items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/c8p3vw: For seven months, Ukrainian troops of the 13th Khartiia Operational Brigade have lived and fought inside an old Soviet gas pipeline near Kupyansk, crawling through a passage just over a metre wide. The BBC became the first international broadcaster to film inside it. Fighters go underground because drones now fill the skies above, making surface movement deadly and stalling advances on both sides.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1: An Iraqi court, the Karkh Criminal Court, sentenced six French nationals to life in prison for joining ISIL, bringing the total convicted in this case to 16, almost all given life terms. The trials, which began in September, cover 47 French citizens transferred from Syria last year. Iraq has taken in thousands of ISIL detainees from dozens of countries since the US handed them over from Syria, and its courts have handed down hundreds of life sentences and executions.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n: Judges at the International Court of Justice, including Nobel peace prize winner Navi Pillay, fear US sanctions if the court rules Thursday that Myanmar's government committed genocide against the Rohingya. The ICJ has never before found a state guilty of genocide, which requires proving intent to destroy a group, as seen in 2016-17 violence in Rakhine state. A Myanmar ruling could set a precedent for how the same court judges Israel's actions in Gaza, so judges have taken advice on protecting their assets from US retaliation.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c32l: Ukrainian troops have spent seven months fighting Russian forces inside an old Soviet gas pipeline in the Kharkiv region, a cramped tunnel just over a metre wide. Going underground, described by one soldier as the 'only option', keeps them safe from drones that now dominate the skies and have stalled advances on both sides. Reaching the tunnel itself requires a dangerous overland journey across open fields under threat of drone attack.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/1: Seventeen US lawmakers, including Representatives Delia Ramirez, Jesus Garcia and Analilia Mejia, are pushing the stalled Living Wage For All Act, which would gradually raise the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour and end the lower tipped minimum wage, with timelines varying by employer size. Incoming congressman Brad Lander plans to co-sponsor it in January. Backing the push, 78% of voters called the minimum wage an important election issue, showing the policy's political momentum.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n: Leaked documents suggest the European Commission exaggerated how well Egypt met welfare targets needed to unlock €2.5bn of a €7.4bn aid package promised to President Abdel Fatah al-Sisi in 2024. The deal aimed to prop up Egypt's economy and curb migration to Europe. The accusation adds pressure on the EU's partnership with Cairo, which also faces criticism over jailed journalists and the closure of independent media, including factchecking outlet Matsadaash and editor Lina Attalah's conviction.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck9d: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met for the first time in over a year in Shenzhen, China, ahead of Thursday's first-ever joint talks between Trump, Putin and Xi Jinping at the APEC summit. Trump and Putin are also expected to hold separate one-on-one talks that could touch on the Ukraine war. The summit's agenda reportedly includes Ukraine, Iran, nuclear proliferation and trade, making it a closely watched moment in US-China-Russia relations.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: Flash flooding turned streets and parking lots into rivers in Davie, Florida, trapping cars and leaving drivers in dangerous conditions. Broward County has declared a state of emergency in response.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n: Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece plan to open an offshore 'return hub' in Rwanda for migrants who have exhausted appeals against deportation from Europe, using a newly agreed EU returns law. Officials hope to send about 100 people there from early next year as a pilot. Critics call the scheme a 'grave moral failing,' and it is expected to face legal challenges as the EU tightens migration policy.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw8r: Israeli ground forces launched a rare operation east of the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, outside the territory Israel already controls, saying it targeted a 'terror tunnel' near the Yellow Line boundary. Hamas called it a 'flagrant violation' of the October 2025 ceasefire. The incursion adds to 13 months of near-daily strikes and dire conditions for Gaza's 2.1 million residents, highlighting how fragile the ceasefire remains.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/t: The United Economic Forum has signed an MoU with IIT-Madras for the Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave on December 8, 2026, aimed at boosting industry-academia collaboration and investment across 10 sectors including EVs, semiconductors, AI, textiles and renewable energy.
items.https://indianexpress.com/article/india/: Security forces in Kashmir's Kulgam district killed Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat, described as the last active local militant in the Valley, after a two-day search of local mosques. Police had learned he was hiding in a mosque attic in Zanglipora and closed in after a tip from a local villager. The operation ends a manhunt that had lasted almost a year.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/set-to-v: Pakistan's Climate Minister Musadik Malik, who earlier this year warned India would have its hands 'cut off' over water aggression, is set to visit India for an SCO meeting. He had urged India to honour the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty, which Delhi suspended after the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: PM Narendra Modi chaired a council of ministers meeting and called for a concerted campaign to eradicate drug abuse, calling it a major social evil, especially among young people. He compared it to past government pushes against left-wing extremism and poverty. The government has stepped up anti-drug messaging recently, particularly in poll-bound Punjab, with leaders like Amit Shah making it a campaign focus.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/c: Panjab University climbed 24 places to joint 150th in the Times Higher Education Interdisciplinary Science Rankings 2027, with its score rising to 55.0 from 52.8 last year. The 2027 edition assessed 1,058 institutions across 102 countries, up from 911 institutions previously. Vice-Chancellor Meenakshi Goyal credited the rise to stronger cross-disciplinary research and collaboration among faculty and students.
items.https://indianexpress.com/article/india/: The NIA arrested Surinder Singh alias Thikriwal, linked to the banned Khalistan Zindabad Force, after the US deported him over the April 26 blast on a Punjab freight rail line between Shambhu and Rajpura. He is the eighth person arrested in the case, which officials say aimed to disrupt communal harmony. Thikriwal had reportedly posted a video glorifying the attack and backing the accused who died carrying it out.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/grand-th: Grand Theft Auto VI has launched in India, with over $1 billion in global pre-orders positioning it to break entertainment sales records. The long-awaited release returns players to Vice City with a new, larger setting after years of anticipation.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: GTA 6 officially launched in India at midnight, 13 years after GTA V, returning players to Vice City and a new, larger state called Leonida. The game needs up to 212GB of storage and is console-only for now, with no PC release date set. In India it costs ₹5,999 for the Standard edition and ₹7,499 for Ultimate on PlayStation.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/b: Eight armed robbers on three motorcycles looted jewellery worth more than ₹30 crore in broad daylight from a shop in Bettiah, Bihar, tying up staff and assaulting two of them, including a guard. One robber reportedly warned staff before leaving that 'the film is yet to come.' The showroom's owner is a leader of the ruling Janata Dal (United), and local BJP leader Renu Devi visited the scene.
items.https://indianexpress.com/article/india/: A financial dispute in Odisha's Boudh district ended in the murder of 31-year-old trader Birupakhya Agrawal, whose body with a slit throat was found in a forest five days after he went missing. Police arrested three people but say the alleged mastermind, teacher Swadhin Pradhan, remains at large after an earlier failed attempt on Agrawal's life. Technical surveillance helped police trace the suspects.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: Maharashtra led India in passenger vehicle sales with 165,000 units in the July-September quarter, while Uttar Pradesh topped two-wheeler sales with 789,000 units, 12.3% of the national total. Total passenger vehicle sales across India reached 13.61 lakh units in the quarter. Western India dominated three of the four vehicle segments, while the south led in three-wheelers with 96,000 units.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Tata Sons' board will meet next week, its first since September 17, to discuss a potential listing that could become India's largest-ever IPO. Once a direction is set, the process could take six to eight months to complete.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/us-ju: A US judge refused to dismiss former JPMorgan banker Chirayu Rana's sexual harassment and discrimination lawsuit, which also accuses the bank of tolerating coercion and racist remarks against him. Rana alleges colleague Lorna Hajdini coerced him into sex; she has countersued for defamation. Judge Lewis Kaplan told both sides to fight the case in court rather than in the media.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said India is on track to hit its $1 trillion export target for 2026-27, after exports grew 16.6% in the first half of this fiscal year. India logged record exports of $863 billion last year. Agrawal said the country remains viewed as a reliable trading partner despite global trade uncertainty.
items.https://www.livemint.com/market/foreign-: Foreign holdings of US Treasuries fell by $75.5 billion in September, the sharpest monthly drop in six months, led by China and France selling down their stockpiles. Total foreign holdings now stand at $9.24 trillion, the lowest in a year. Japan, the largest foreign holder, also cut its holdings by $5.2 billion as it sold securities to support the yen, which hit a four-decade low against the dollar.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmy4: UK household energy bills are forecast to rise by £443, or 26%, from January as inflation hit its highest rate in a year at 3.6%, driven partly by fuel costs from the US-Israel-Iran conflict. The Bank of England already raised interest rates this month, from 3.75% to 4%, and may raise again to meet its 2% inflation target. Some households will get a one-off £100 payment announced in the Budget to offset the increase.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: Vedanta Group is exploring using AI for geological analysis and mineral block modelling, which it says could cut exploration timelines from three to four months down to just six to seven days.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Tata Sons board members, including chairman N Chandrasekaran and Noel Tata, are visiting Air India's Gurugram headquarters to review the loss-making airline's performance, with CEO Tewolde Gebremariam presenting. Discussions are likely to cover the operational integration of Air India and Air India Express. Air India, co-owned by Tata Sons and Singapore Airlines (25.1% stake), faces headwinds from fuel costs and the Pakistan airspace closure hitting long-haul routes.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/sells: Analysts pushed back on a short-seller report from Spruce Point Capital, which flagged risks at fast-fashion retailer Groupe Dynamite and predicted a 35-70% stock downside over supplier and inventory concerns. Dynamite shares rose about 2% after the report, recovering part of a 12% drop the day before. Analysts at Bank of Montreal and Stifel called the sell-off overdone and questioned the report's timing given the stock's known slowdown.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: India and the US are nearing completion of trade deal negotiations, with legal texts almost finalized, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said. However, signing depends on new US tariff rules being set and ongoing Section 301 investigations being resolved. The deal's timing matters for Indian exporters facing tariff and visa pressures in the US market.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/pb-fintech-cofoun: PB Fintech cofounder Alok Bansal is stepping down as executive vice-chairman and whole-time director when his term ends on March 31, 2027, moving to a non-executive board role instead. Bansal, an IIM Calcutta alumnus who cofounded Policybazaar in 2008, cited a personal desire to leave executive duties. His exit joins a wider wave of founders departing startups this year, including from Unacademy, BigBasket and Setu.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: The Trump administration is reportedly discussing a rule that would force US companies to disclose their use of Chinese AI models. The plan, discussed by the Treasury Department and the White House science office, would reportedly apply to firms like Airbnb, which uses Alibaba's Qwen model for its AI customer service.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/botsync-raises-11: Singapore-based robotics startup Botsync raised $11 million led by IvyCap Ventures, taking its total funding past $20 million. Its software lets factories coordinate robots from different vendors alongside existing machinery, automating floors without replacing equipment. The funds will go toward predictive maintenance features, improving its mobile robots, and expanding its India team to support global deployments.
items.https://entrackr.com/news/physical-ai-st: Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs raised $47 million in Series A funding, split between $26 million in equity led by Accel and $21 million in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton. Founded in 2026 by former Nazara CEO Manish Agarwal and Ishank Gupta, the startup collects real-world data on how people perform everyday tasks to train AI and robotics systems. Other investors included Prosus Ventures and Bajaj-linked funds.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: US and South Korean authorities issued urgent cybersecurity advisories over newly found vulnerabilities in the Java programming language, urging users to install security updates immediately.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/humyn-labs-raises: Physical AI startup Humyn Labs raised $47 million, comprising $26 million in Series A equity led by Accel and $21 million in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton. The company, founded by former Nazara CEO Manish Agarwal and Ishank Gupta, says it has already crossed $50 million in annualised revenue within six months. It will use the funds to expand robot deployment and data collection to Brazil, South Korea and India.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: India left pacer Mohammed Siraj and spinner Ravindra Jadeja out of the opening Test against New Zealand. India chose to bowl first after winning the toss on a green pitch, asking New Zealand to bat.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/arti: Fresh claims from Cameron Bancroft, the player who tampered with the ball in South Africa in 2018, have deepened the long-running sandpaper scandal rocking Australian cricket. In a 4,000-word account, Bancroft alleges all Australian players and coaches present in Cape Town knew of the plot, backing earlier claims by Usman Khawaja, David Warner and Chadd Sayers. Captain Pat Cummins has denied Khawaja's version, keeping the controversy alive eight years on.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/i: India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and chose to field first in the opening Test against New Zealand at Wellington's Basin Reserve, continuing his unbeaten toss record on the tour. India left out pacer Mohammed Siraj and spinner Ravindra Jadeja, picking Washington Sundar as the lone spinner alongside four pacers: Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj. New Zealand kept its unchanged XI.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: New Zealand captain Tom Latham says the team is being flexible with managing its fast bowlers' workloads, given ten Tests scheduled in quick succession. He hopes the squad can look back on the stretch satisfied with how it was handled.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art: With the Premier League resuming after 10 games, Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Manchester United sit in the relegation zone, and history suggests this is already a cause for concern. Palace and United return with new managers, Thomas Frank and Mauricio Pochettino respectively, while Sunderland has stuck with Regis le Bris. Since the league expanded to 20 teams in 1995-96, only one of three bottom-placed sides after 10 games has typically avoided relegation, in 19 of 31 seasons (61%).
items.https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editori: The Hindu's editorial argues India must play at its best in its two-Test series against New Zealand, a traditionally tough away assignment with testing pitch and weather conditions. India has already won the T20I and ODI legs of the tour. With India fourth in the World Test Championship table and hopes of a final berth fragile, strong results here and against Australia next year are crucial, especially for a batting lineup without Rohit Sharma.
items.https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026: Internal Meta chats, revealed by Reuters, show staff raising alarms about the company's Muse AI agent accessing private messages users never expected it to review and mixing up details between different users' conversations. In one case Muse referenced a coffee table pickup from someone else's chat, and in another it unexpectedly sent a definition of 'money laundering.' Employees flagged a possible 'cross-account context leak,' highlighting the privacy risks of deploying AI agents inside messaging platforms.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: MIT Technology Review's AI Hype Index notes how pervasive AI has become, from Google's AI Overviews costing it billions in lost ad revenue to humanoid robots being used for cleaning and AI-assisted cyberattacks disrupting everyday life. It points to cultural saturation too, including a biopic of Sam Altman and an AI-altered version of The Odyssey. The piece is a critical look at how AI hype often outpaces its real capabilities, ten years after AlphaGo's famous win.
items.https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2026/11/w: Game designer Will Wright, creator of SimCity and The Sims, is developing MyMems, a new generative-AI game that mines players' personal memories to create digital people who can team up to solve puzzles. Built with studio Gallium and partner Artificial Agency, it marks Wright's first major project since 2008's Spore. It reflects a wider trend of game studios using AI to build personalized, player-generated content rather than scripted worlds.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: AI startup Osmo, working near Newark Airport, has about 30 human experts cataloguing smells and cross-referencing them with chemical data to train what it calls the first foundation model for scent. Founder Alex Wiltschko says the model has reached 'human-level olfactory intelligence,' matching average humans at detecting and distinguishing odors. The approach shows how AI is expanding beyond text and images into senses like smell, which the founder says is central to memory and emotion.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/18/palmer: Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey warned at the New York Times DealBook Summit that AI-powered cyberattacks are advancing faster than outdated systems can defend against, pointing to a recent wave of tech outages. He said AI is helping adversaries, including North Korea, discover and exploit new vulnerabilities for both strategic and financial gain. His comments underscore growing pressure on companies and governments to modernize cybersecurity as AI lowers the barrier to launching sophisticated attacks.
items.https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/11/: At its Ignite conference, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella unveiled Word, Excel and PowerPoint running inside Copilot, which he called 'the new OS for work,' with files still editable in the original Office apps. The shift flips the usual model, making AI agents the primary interface while traditional software becomes a supporting layer, drawing on emails, calendars, chats and files. It builds on Microsoft's September Copilot redesign, adding autonomous agents and new governance tools as the next phase.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: MIT Technology Review's research roundup covers how today's AI still hasn't matched the breakthrough behind AlphaGo's win over Lee Sedol a decade ago, an interview with AI safety researcher Nick Cammarata, scrutiny of inflated AGI claims, and the rise of personal AI assistants reshaping how the internet is used.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/18/sam-al: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he isn't bothered by actor Andrew Garfield portraying him in the upcoming film 'Artificial,' which covers OpenAI's rise and his brief 2023 ouster, calling it not even among the top ten weirdest things about his life. The comedy-drama opens in theaters on Christmas. It follows a wave of Silicon Valley-inspired films and shows, including documentaries on Elizabeth Holmes and Sam Bankman-Fried, reflecting Hollywood's growing interest in tech industry scandals.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/18/nvidia: Nvidia surprised investors by announcing it would delay filing its routine quarterly SEC report, the 10-Q, without explaining why, prompting an analyst to call it a 'red flag.' Interim CEO Colette Kress said the filing would come 'in the coming weeks.' Analysts suspect the delay relates to how much Nvidia must disclose about its ongoing investigation into former CEO Jensen Huang, since the 10-Q covers legal proceedings and risk factors in more detail than the earnings release.
items.https://www.theverge.com/tech/1035924/nv: Nvidia now generates roughly $8,300 in pure profit every second, illustrating its scale even after the turmoil around founder CEO Jensen Huang's resignation. The piece argues Nvidia's financial dominance is now so vast that rivals AMD, Intel and Qualcomm barely register as competitors. It frames recent leadership upheaval as unlikely to meaningfully threaten the company given the sheer size of its profits and market position.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: Following Jensen Huang's exit as Nvidia CEO over an affair tied to a Chinese spying investigation, interim CEO Colette Kress held her first earnings call, and the piece notes a shift in tone. As former CFO, Kress had reportedly pushed back on Huang's heavy spending to finance customers, a disciplining role she may now extend as the person actually running the roughly $3 trillion company. It questions how dependent the broader AI boom is on one individual leader.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: A petition to reinstate ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has gathered over 115,000 signatures, including Elon Musk and prominent open-source AI figures from Hugging Face and venture firms Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia. Many signatories have a financial stake in open-source AI models that can be downloaded and run independently of big tech companies, which Huang had publicly championed. The episode highlights how leadership changes at chipmakers can ripple into broader debates over AI concentration and openness.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: Despite OpenAI pausing a major frontier training run this summer after its AI agents reportedly hacked Hugging Face, and Anthropic's Dario Amodei warning in September about slowing the most powerful models, Nvidia and AMD's latest earnings show booming chip demand unaffected by any pullback. The piece argues that even if AI labs ease off building ever-larger frontier models, chipmakers' near-term business looks resilient. It highlights a disconnect between AI safety caution among top labs and continued hardware investment.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/18/palmer: Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey said Nvidia's board handed China a win by ousting longtime CEO Jensen Huang, arguing the move weakens America's position in chip competition and contributed to a roughly $1 trillion drop in Nvidia's market value. Luckey wants Huang reinstated, even though he disagrees with Huang's push to allow more chip exports to China. He argued Chinese chipmakers stand to gain ground against Nvidia from the leadership instability.
items.https://www.theverge.com/policy/1036749/: President Trump, facing opposition to AI data center and chip fab plans at home, is pursuing the Philippines, a former US colony, as a site to build them instead. His visit drew both celebratory welcomes and street protests against the initiative, dubbed 'Pax Silica,' which aims to secure chips and critical minerals used in AI hardware. The move reflects the US pushing AI infrastructure expansion overseas amid domestic pushback.
items.https://www.theverge.com/policy/1036935/: With weeks left in 2026, US lawmakers are racing to pass protections against online harms like deepfakes and grooming before year-end. A Senate Judiciary hearing targeted Roblox for using forced arbitration clauses to block lawsuits from users, including minors, allegedly groomed on the platform. Separately, Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Laurel Lee pushed the Defiance Act with Paris Hilton's backing, which would let victims of nonconsensual deepfakes sue their creators directly in court.
items.https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026: A nonprofit called the Tech Oversight Project put up DC billboards accusing both ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and the Trump administration of being compromised, as Congress faces pressure to investigate their ties. Trump has backed a campaign to reinstate Huang, despite many Republicans calling it a bad idea, while Nvidia's board says reinstatement isn't being considered amid an ongoing probe into Chinese spying allegations against Huang. Huang said he would be 'honored' to return and affirmed his loyalty to the US.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/18/anthro: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its initial $70-78 range, valuing the AI company at $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis as it begins trading on Nasdaq under ticker 'ANT.' That's well above the $965 billion valuation from its last private round in May but below the $2 trillion it had reportedly once targeted. Strong demand came despite recent AI market jitters following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure, and its debut will be watched as a signal for rival OpenAI's own future plans.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/soket-ai-raises-4: Indian AI startup Soket AI raised $4 million from Bajaj Finserv's Finserv Intelligence and Pennant Technologies to build sovereign, India-focused foundation models. Backed by the government's IndiaAI Mission, Soket recently launched EKA-1, a 26-billion-parameter model under its Project EKA initiative focused on math, coding and reasoning in Indian languages. Founded in 2019 by Abhishek Upperwal, the funding supports India's push for homegrown AI infrastructure independent of foreign providers.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being woven into India's manufacturing, infrastructure and transportation sectors, a shift expected to boost productivity and sustainability. Companies adopting industrial AI are likely to see shorter engineering timelines as the technology scales across factories and infrastructure projects.
items.https://inc42.com/features/ais-social-la: As AI assistants increasingly replace search engines, social networks and marketplaces as the way people discover information and products, startups built around clicks, engagement and ads face a new battle for visibility and revenue. The piece explores how platforms dependent on search traffic and algorithmic distribution could lose influence as AI takes over recommendations and decision-making. It frames this emerging 'agent-driven internet' as a structural challenge for the existing web ecosystem, including in India's startup scene.
